observations: expect_prompt only allocates a cancellation ticket. SessionStarted and local turn seq precede the prompt transport and are not successful-handoff signals.
RpcConnection::call registers the request waiter, writes JSONRPC through write_line, then waits for a matching response. The successful local handoff point is after write_line Ok and before rx.recv.

write_line serializes, appends newline, performs write_all and returns flush. Production writer is ChildStdin. This proves only local write/flush success, not ACP parse/accept, cloud execution or completion.
A stopped ticket or session-open failure can return before session/prompt is written. A later RPC error or stdout closure can follow successful write and cause a failed turn.
Write/flush failure gives no confirmed handoff; partial bytes may nevertheless have reached the child.

RPC request ids are connection-local, not global across restarts. Existing checkpoint turn ids are not passed to the provider prompt. A request-owned IPC channel retains caller correlation without relying on the current chat, ticket, seq or rpc id.

Current native command resolves after turn completion and may return Rust Ok containing failed/cancelled/superseded outcomes. No current event exposes prompt write success. App.emit failure is ignored on the existing event path.
